message.content:
The sculpture that most people think of when they picture the 19th‑century art world is **Auguste Rodin’s “The Thinker”** (originally conceived in 1880–1881, first cast in 1902). Even though its first public casts appeared just after the century ended, the idea and the original models were created in the late 1800s, making it a quintessential product of that era.  

Other major 19th‑century works include:

| Artist | Sculpture | Year |
|--------|-----------|------|
| Auguste Rodin | “The Kiss” | 1889 |
| Auguste Rodin | “The Gates of Hell” (series) | 1880s–1890s |
| Michelangelo Buonarroti | “David” (though Renaissance, still hugely influential) | 1504 |

But if you’re looking for the single piece that has become almost synonymous with 19th‑century sculpture, “The Thinker” is the one that dominates popular imagination.
